Acute COPD exacerbation / infection.description: Acute worsening of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease symptoms, often infection-triggered.
first_line_approach: Antibiotics if infective exacerbation criteria are met
clinical_considerations: Confirm smoking status and prior COPD diagnosis before treatment escalation.
Chronic steroid use has long-term risks -- courses should be short.

Acute dystonic reactions.description: Sudden abnormal, sustained muscle contractions, usually from antipsychotic or antiemetic medication exposure.
first_line_approach: Identify and stop the causative medication
clinical_considerations: Medication history is essential -- this is drug-induced, not a primary illness.

Acute laryngitis.description: Inflammation of the larynx, usually viral, causing hoarseness.
monitoring: Symptom duration beyond 2-3 weeks warrants ENT referral
clinical_considerations: Antibiotics are not indicated for typical viral laryngitis.

Acute otitis media.description: Middle ear infection, common in children, causing ear pain and possible fever.
first_line_approach: Watchful waiting or antibiotics depending on age/severity per guideline
clinical_considerations: Antibiotic decision depends on age and severity criteria not captured here -- clinical evaluation required.

Acute pulmonary edema.description: Fluid accumulation in the lungs, typically from acute heart failure -- a medical emergency.
clinical_considerations: This is an emergency presentation -- Module 3 does not recommend outpatient medication management.

Acute rhinosinusitis.description: Short-duration sinus inflammation, usually viral, sometimes bacterial.
first_line_approach: Antibiotics only if bacterial criteria (severe/persistent/worsening) are met
clinical_considerations: Most cases are viral and self-limited; antibiotics are frequently over-used for this condition.

Allergic sinusitis.description: Sinus inflammation driven by allergic response.
clinical_considerations: Consider allergy testing if recurrent or seasonal pattern is reported.

Anaphylaxis.description: Severe, rapid-onset systemic allergic reaction -- a life-threatening emergency.
red_flags: Any suspected anaphylaxis is itself the red flag
clinical_considerations: Module 3 cannot substitute for emergency epinephrine administration -- this profile exists for post-emergency education/follow-up only.

Anemia.description: Reduced red blood cell mass/hemoglobin, with many possible underlying causes.
first_line_approach: Identify underlying cause (iron/B12/folate deficiency, chronic disease, bleeding, etc.)
clinical_considerations: Treatment is entirely dependent on the underlying cause -- supplementation without a confirmed deficiency is not appropriate.
relevant_module1_observations: Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Automated count

Atrial fibrillation.description: Irregular, often rapid heart rhythm originating in the atria.
first_line_approach: Stroke risk assessment and anticoagulation if indicated
clinical_considerations: Anticoagulation decisions require a formal stroke-risk score (e.g. CHA2DS2-VASc) -- not automated here.

Boerhaave.description: Spontaneous esophageal rupture, usually from forceful vomiting -- a surgical emergency.
red_flags: Any suspected case is itself the red flag
clinical_considerations: This condition requires emergency surgical evaluation -- outpatient management is not appropriate.

Bronchiectasis.description: Chronic, irreversible dilation of the bronchi leading to recurrent infection and mucus production.
clinical_considerations: Long-term pulmonology follow-up is standard for this chronic condition.

Bronchiolitis.description: Viral lower respiratory infection, primarily affecting infants.
medication_classes: Supportive care only (no proven specific medication in most cases)
clinical_considerations: Bronchodilators and antibiotics are generally not indicated for typical viral bronchiolitis.

Bronchitis.description: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, usually viral.
clinical_considerations: Most acute bronchitis is viral; antibiotics do not shorten typical courses.

Bronchospasm / acute asthma exacerbation.description: Acute narrowing of the airways causing wheeze and breathlessness.
clinical_considerations: Severe exacerbations require urgent in-person evaluation, not remote guidance alone.

Chagas.description: Chronic infection with Trypanosoma cruzi, which can cause cardiac and GI complications over years.
first_line_approach: Antiparasitic treatment in acute/early chronic phase
clinical_considerations: Specialist infectious-disease and cardiology involvement is standard.

first_line_approach: Identify and treat contributing allergy/structural causes
medication_classes: Short antibiotic course for acute-on-chronic flares
red_flags: Severe facial pain with neurological signs
clinical_considerations: ENT referral is appropriate for persistent or recurrent cases.

Cluster headache.description: Severe, recurrent unilateral headaches occurring in clusters.
clinical_considerations: New-onset severe headache patterns should be evaluated to exclude secondary causes before assuming cluster headache.

Croup.description: Viral upper airway infection in young children causing a barking cough and stridor.
clinical_considerations: Moderate-to-severe croup needs in-person urgent evaluation.

Ebola.description: Severe viral hemorrhagic fever requiring immediate isolation and specialized care.
red_flags: Any suspected case is itself the red flag -- public-health emergency
clinical_considerations: Suspected cases require immediate isolation and public-health notification -- this is entirely outside outpatient/self-management scope.

Epiglottitis.description: Life-threatening inflammation/infection of the epiglottis that can rapidly obstruct the airway.
red_flags: Any suspected case is itself the red flag
clinical_considerations: Suspected epiglottitis requires emergency in-person airway management -- never manage remotely.

GERD.description: Gastroesophageal reflux disease -- backward flow of stomach acid causing heartburn/regurgitation.
clinical_considerations: Elevated or rising BMI is a relevant, modifiable contributing factor worth highlighting.

Guillain-Barré syndrome.description: Autoimmune condition causing rapidly progressive muscle weakness -- can be life-threatening.
clinical_considerations: This condition can progress to respiratory failure within days -- urgent in-person evaluation is required, not outpatient management.

HIV (initial infection).description: Acute retroviral syndrome following initial HIV infection.
first_line_approach: Prompt linkage to HIV specialist care
Early antiretroviral therapy per current guidelines
clinical_considerations: Diagnosis and ART initiation must be confirmed and managed by a specialist -- not appropriate for local knowledge-base guidance alone.

Influenza.description: Viral respiratory infection with systemic symptoms (fever, myalgia, cough).
first_line_approach: Antiviral therapy if within treatment window and indicated
clinical_considerations: Antivirals are most effective when started within 48 hours of symptom onset.

Inguinal hernia.description: Protrusion of abdominal contents through the inguinal canal.
first_line_approach: Watchful waiting for small, asymptomatic, reducible hernias in select cases
clinical_considerations: Definitive treatment is surgical -- medication is not a substitute for surgical evaluation.

Larygospasm.description: Sudden, involuntary spasm of the vocal cords causing temporary airway obstruction.
first_line_approach: Address triggering cause (e.g. reflux, irritant exposure)
Emergency care if not rapidly self-resolving
medication_classes: Address underlying trigger (e.g. reflux therapy if GERD-related)
red_flags: Episode not resolving within a minute
clinical_considerations: Recurrent laryngospasm warrants ENT evaluation for underlying cause.

Localized edema.description: Localized fluid accumulation, with causes ranging from venous insufficiency to renal, hepatic, or cardiac disease.
red_flags: Sudden unilateral leg swelling with pain (possible DVT)
clinical_considerations: Edema has many distinct causes -- kidney/liver/cardiac markers from Module 1 are relevant context, not a diagnosis.

Myasthenia gravis.description: Autoimmune neuromuscular condition causing fluctuating muscle weakness.
clinical_considerations: Myasthenic crisis is a medical emergency requiring immediate care.

Myocarditis.description: Inflammation of the heart muscle, often viral, which can impair cardiac function.
first_line_approach: Supportive heart-failure-directed therapy if function impaired
red_flags: Signs of heart failure or arrhythmia
clinical_considerations: Requires cardiology evaluation -- outpatient medication alone is not sufficient for active myocarditis.

PSVT.description: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia -- episodes of rapid, regular heart rate.
first_line_approach: Rate-control or antiarrhythmic medication for recurrent episodes
red_flags: Chest pain, fainting, or hemodynamic instability during an episode
clinical_considerations: Recurrent episodes warrant cardiology/electrophysiology referral.

Pancreatic neoplasm.description: Mass/tumor of the pancreas requiring oncologic evaluation.
medication_classes: Managed entirely by oncology/surgery -- not appropriate for a general medication-class list
monitoring: Glucose/HbA1c (new-onset diabetes can be an early sign)
red_flags: New-onset diabetes in an older adult
clinical_considerations: Suspected neoplasm requires urgent specialist referral, not primary-care medication management.

Panic attack.description: Sudden episode of intense fear with physical symptoms (palpitations, dyspnea, dizziness).
first_line_approach: Short-term or maintenance medication if recurrent/disabling
red_flags: Chest pain not clearly explained by panic (must exclude cardiac cause)
clinical_considerations: Cardiac causes of similar symptoms should be excluded before attributing chest symptoms to panic alone.

Pericarditis.description: Inflammation of the pericardium (sac around the heart), typically causing sharp chest pain.
first_line_approach: Colchicine as adjunct to reduce recurrence
clinical_considerations: Complicated or recurrent pericarditis requires cardiology involvement.

Pneumonia.description: Infection of the lung parenchyma, bacterial or viral.
first_line_approach: Antibiotics for bacterial pneumonia per severity/setting
clinical_considerations: Severity assessment (e.g. CURB-65-type criteria) determines outpatient vs. inpatient management -- not automated here.

Possible NSTEMI / STEMI.description: Suspected acute myocardial infarction -- a time-critical medical emergency.
first_line_approach: Emergency cardiology evaluation and reperfusion therapy
red_flags: Any suspected case is itself the red flag
clinical_considerations: This is a time-critical emergency -- Module 3 should never delay emergency care with outpatient-style guidance.

Pulmonary embolism.description: Blockage of a pulmonary artery, usually by a blood clot -- a life-threatening emergency.
red_flags: Any suspected case is itself the red flag
clinical_considerations: Requires emergency evaluation and imaging -- not manageable through outpatient guidance.

Pulmonary neoplasm.description: Mass/tumor of the lung requiring oncologic evaluation.
medication_classes: Managed entirely by oncology/pulmonology -- not appropriate for a general medication-class list
clinical_considerations: Suspected neoplasm requires urgent specialist referral.

SLE.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus -- a chronic autoimmune disease affecting multiple organ systems.
red_flags: Signs of organ involvement (renal, cardiac, neurological)
clinical_considerations: Rheumatology management is standard; kidney markers from Module 1 are particularly relevant given common renal involvement.
relevant_module1_observations: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count
Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

Sarcoidosis.description: Inflammatory condition causing granuloma formation, most often affecting the lungs.
clinical_considerations: Many cases are mild and self-limited; treatment intensity depends on organ involvement.

Scombroid food poisoning.description: Histamine-toxin reaction from improperly stored fish, mimicking an allergic reaction.
clinical_considerations: Distinguishing this from true food allergy/anaphylaxis matters for future exposure counseling.

Spontaneous pneumothorax.description: Collapse of part of the lung due to air in the pleural space without trauma.
first_line_approach: Observation or chest tube depending on size/severity
red_flags: Sudden chest pain with shortness of breath
Any suspected case is itself a red flag
clinical_considerations: Requires emergency imaging and possible procedural intervention -- not medication-managed.

Spontaneous rib fracture.description: Rib fracture occurring without significant trauma, often from an underlying bone-weakening process.
first_line_approach: Evaluate for underlying cause (e.g. osteoporosis, bone lesion)
Encourage deep breathing to prevent pneumonia
red_flags: Signs of pneumothorax or significant respiratory compromise
clinical_considerations: 'Spontaneous' fracture should prompt investigation for an underlying bone-weakening cause.

Stable angina.description: Predictable exertional chest discomfort from reduced blood flow to the heart muscle.
first_line_approach: Cardiology evaluation for further risk stratification
red_flags: Chest pain at rest or with minimal exertion (possible unstable angina)
clinical_considerations: Lipid, glucose, and blood-pressure trends from Module 1 are directly relevant to cardiovascular risk modification here.

Tuberculosis.description: Mycobacterial infection, most often pulmonary, requiring prolonged multi-drug therapy.
clinical_considerations: Requires specialist/public-health management -- not appropriate for local knowledge-base-only guidance.
relevant_module1_observations: Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma
Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma

URTI.description: Upper respiratory tract infection -- the common cold, almost always viral.
clinical_considerations: Antibiotics are not indicated for typical viral URTI.

Unstable angina.description: Chest pain at rest or with minimal exertion, representing acute coronary syndrome risk.
red_flags: Any suspected case is itself the red flag
clinical_considerations: Requires emergency evaluation -- do not delay care with outpatient-style guidance.

Viral pharyngitis.description: Viral throat infection causing sore throat, usually self-limited.
clinical_considerations: Rapid strep testing should guide antibiotic decisions rather than empiric treatment.

Whooping cough.description: Pertussis -- a bacterial respiratory infection causing paroxysmal coughing fits.
first_line_approach: Isolate from vulnerable contacts (infants, pregnant individuals)
clinical_considerations: Post-exposure prophylaxis for close contacts should be considered -- this is a public-health-relevant infection.
